cleanIR.title: Band 13 - Clean Infrared
cleanIR.help: Band 13 at 10.3 µm is an infrared window, meaning it is not strongly affected by atmospheric water vapor absorption. This channel is useful for detecting clouds all times of day and night and is particularly useful in retrievals of cloud top height. 10.3 µm - Clean Longwave IR Window Band - 2 km resolution
cleanIR.time: All timestamps are given in Zulu time (UTC/GMT)

visibleRed.title: Band 02 - Visible Red
visibleRed.help: Visible band 2 is in the red portion of the spectrum and has the highest resolution of any ABI band at 0.5 km, and for that reason is the primary visible band. It is used primarily to monitor the evolution of clouds throughout the daylight hours. 0.64 µm - Red Band - 0.5 km resolution
visibleRed.time: All timestamps are given in Zulu time (UTC/GMT)

waterVapor.title: Band 08 - Water Vapor
waterVapor.help: Band 8 will be used for upper-level tropospheric water vapor tracking, jet stream identification, hurricane track forecasting, mid-latitude storm forecasting, severe weather analysis, upper mid-level moisture estimation (for legacy vertical moisture profiles) and turbulence detection. 6.2 µm - Upper-level Water Vapor Band - 2 km resolution
waterVapor.time: This band shows atmospheric temperatures in Celsius. Values in the red to yellow range represent a dry atmosphere. Values between yellow and white, including blue, represent a relatively moist atmosphere. Values colder than white, including green, represent clouds
